newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ayala Land outlines development strategy.
newsitem.headline: Ayala Land outlines development strategy.

text.p: Ayala Land Inc, the country's top real estate firm, said on Wednesday it was realigning its strategy and budgeting 10 billion pesos in capital spending this year despite worries of a slowdown in the property sector.
Company officials said the thrust would be on new investments in areas such as middle-income housing and infrastructure, and on developments outside Metro Manila.
Last year, Ayala Land planned to spend a similar amount but in the end only spent half the amount because of concerns over a possible glut in office space and high-priced apartments.
"We're putting a lot of emphasis on the middle-income housing market. There's tremendous demand for that sector," Ayala Land vice-chairman Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala told Reuters.
"We're readjusting our portfolio. There's a very strong regional thrust in...Ayala Land right now," Zobel said.
"We're trying to expand out portfolio base and emphasize areas that are growing and de-emphasize areas where supply is a little bit stronger than demand," he added.

"We anticipate an oversupply in some sectors of the market such as high-end residential condominiums, and the high-end offices in the central business district of Makati," Francisco Licuanan, the firm's president, told reporters.
He added the oversupply may come about in 1999.
In his speech to stockholders, Licuanan said its Laguna Technopark will introduce a 90-hectare expansion site this year to meet demand for industrial lots south of Manila.
Ayala Land had also concluded a joint venture agreement to develop a shopping centre in Laguna, south of Manila.

In central Philippines, the company has drawn up plans for another mixed-use development in Cebu city, the 24-hectare Cebu Civic and Trade Center which will have office and residential buildings, retail centers and a hotel, Licuanan said.
In Metro Manila, Ayala Land said it had identified niche markets such as luxury service apartments.
It will also expand the leasable area of its main shopping area, the Ayala Center, by 28,000 square metres. This is expected to be completed in 1998.
Overseas, Ayala Land will develop luxury apartments in a prime residential district of Singapore.
On the infrastructure front, Ayala land said it had given unsolicited proposals to the government to build rail-based projects to serve Metro Manila.
